items.text: Rep. Thomas Massie says he will force a House vote next week to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war and other military actions.
items.detail: Massie's eight articles of impeachment say the Iran war violated the War Powers Resolution and that Hegseth ignored civilian-casualty laws. They also cite drug-boat strikes that killed at least 221 people, retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, the seizure of Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores, and an unauthorized war in Yemen. Massie told CNN he will trigger the vote when Congress returns. He said he would drop the effort if Hegseth resigns. As a privileged resolution, it must get floor action within two legislative days, though the House could vote to table it. President Trump said Hegseth is "doing a very good job." A Pentagon spokesman said Hegseth "will not back down."
items.why: A simple House majority would impeach a sitting war-time defense secretary, though removal requires two-thirds of the Senate.

items.text: Two projectiles struck a tanker off northern Qatar overnight, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers and a tug caught fire near Hormuz.
items.detail: The British military's UKMTO said the tanker was hit about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, at 2320 UTC Wednesday. The crew's condition and the extent of the damage were not confirmed. Separately, the IRGC said one tanker hit a mine south of the Strait of Hormuz. It said a supertanker leaving the strait caught fire, and a tug helping it also caught fire. The IRGC said the ships had tried to use unauthorized routes. Qatar is mediating between the U.S. and Iran. A Qatari LNG carrier was hit on Oct. 30.
items.why: Attacks on Gulf shipping keep pressure on oil and gas prices while cease-fire talks continue.

items.text: Medicare finalized its 2027 doctor-pay rule, cutting the basic payment rate about 2% as a one-year 2.5% boost expires.
items.detail: The conversion factor for doctors who do not qualify under alternative payment models drops 2.31%, to $32.63. For doctors who qualify, it drops 1.83%, to $32.95. When an office visit and a minor same-day procedure are billed together, the lower-cost service will be paid at 80%. Starting April 1, 2027, approved ACOs may reduce or waive Part B cost-sharing for many services. The rule also writes into regulation the new law limiting Medicare eligibility to citizens, green-card holders and a few other groups. The rule takes effect Jan. 1, 2027. CMS also finalized its 2027 hospital outpatient and home health payment rules.
items.why: These rates set what Medicare pays doctors next year, which affects access for millions of seniors.

items.text: An Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome diverted to a French military air base Thursday after a bomb threat and landed safely.
items.detail: France's prime minister's office said the Airbus A320 landed at the Evreux base in Normandy. The French air force said it sent jets to escort the plane. Earlier this week, hoax threats against LOT, SAS, Wizz Air and Ryanair flights forced diversions.
items.why: Repeated threats are disrupting European air travel and pulling in military escorts.

items.text: Congress will be controlled by Democrats in January after they won both the House and the Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, AP projected.
items.detail: AP called the Senate for Democrats late Tuesday and the House early Wednesday. Democrats flipped at least seven Republican-held Senate seats: Kansas (Adam Hamilton over Sen. Roger Marshall, the state's first Democratic senator since 1932), Iowa (Josh Turek over Rep. Ashley Hinson), Texas (James Talarico over Ken Paxton), Ohio (Sherrod Brown over Sen. Jon Husted), Maine (Troy Jackson over Sen. Susan Collins), North Carolina (Roy Cooper) and South Carolina (Annie Andrews). They held Georgia (Sen. Jon Ossoff), Michigan (Abdul El-Sayed) and New Hampshire (Chris Pappas). In the House they flipped more than two dozen districts. As of 4 a.m. Eastern, Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi were still uncalled. Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become the first Black House speaker. Trump wrote that he "wasn't on the Ballot," vowed to veto Democratic bills and told Fox News he would accept the results; Senate Majority Leader John Thune vowed to resist the new majority's agenda. The new Congress is sworn in in January.
items.why: Democratic majorities can block Trump's legislation, reject his nominees in the Senate and open investigations of his administration for the last two years of his term.

items.text: Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek to lead House Republicans in the new Congress, setting up a race between Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan.
items.detail: Johnson told staff on a Wednesday morning call and wrote colleagues that the job's demands on his family drove the decision; he is expected to stay in the House as a rank-and-file member from Louisiana, AP reported, citing two people familiar with his decision. Majority Leader Steve Scalise and Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan each announced bids in letters to colleagues. House Republicans plan to elect their leaders Tuesday, Nov. 10, when Democrats will take the majority in January after Tuesday's midterms.
items.why: The next House Republican leader will run the minority's response to a Democratic House expected to open investigations of the Trump administration.

items.text: The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 1,569 points, or 3%, Wednesday, its best day since April 2025, after Democrats won Congress, as oil prices fell.
items.detail: The Dow closed at 53,356.12; the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq composite rose 1.4% to 25,736.51. U.S. crude oil fell more than 7% after Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses, and Treasury yields fell. Bank and retail stocks led; Nvidia, CoreWeave and Tesla fell amid concern over limits on data centers after Democrats' wins, including Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's pledged moratorium.
items.why: Stocks, oil and borrowing costs moved sharply on the election result in a single session.

items.text: The death toll from Russia's bombing of an aid site in Komyshuvakha, Ukraine, rose to 40 Wednesday, with more than 30 people possibly still under rubble, Zelenskyy said.
items.detail: Rescuers have searched for three days after Monday's strikes on a school used to hand out aid and a nearby shelter in the Zaporizhzhia region village. AP called it one of the deadliest strikes in the region in nearly five years of full-scale war; Russia's Defense Ministry said it targeted Ukrainian military units. Russian attacks also caused hours of power and water outages across Kyiv and surrounding regions Wednesday, AP reported.
items.why: It is among the deadliest Russian attacks on civilians in the war.

items.text: Vice President JD Vance said the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms, writing, "The reason we lost is the war."
items.detail: In a long post Wednesday, Vance said many 2024 Trump voters backed Democrats to end the war, over the cost of living, to put America first and to change the U.S. relationship with Israel, and called a suggestion to seek a diplomatic resolution with Iran "sound." Asked about it, President Trump said he agreed the war "drove the gasoline up a little bit, short term" but said he would do it again because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon (Axios, Reuters). Trump also told reporters he is not considering replacing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying "No, I think he's doing a very good job," after CBS News reported, citing multiple sources, that he had asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay.
items.why: It is the clearest break yet inside the administration over the Iran war as Trump weighs whether to resume major combat.

week.text: Governors' offices in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Iowa flipped to Democrats Tuesday, giving the party a majority of governorships for the first time since 2006, AP reported.
week.detail: In Texas, Gina Hinojosa ousted third-term Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming the first Democrat elected statewide there since 1994. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of any U.S. state. Amy Acton beat Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio, and Rob Sand beat Zach Lahn in Iowa. Republicans held Florida, where Byron Donalds became the nation's first Black Republican elected governor. Democratic Govs. Kathy Hochul (N.Y.), Josh Shapiro (Pa.), JB Pritzker (Ill.), Wes Moore (Md.), Maura Healey (Mass.) and Tina Kotek (Ore.) won reelection, and Xavier Becerra won California. Thirty-six states elected governors.
week.why: Governors control state responses to Trump's agenda on the National Guard, immigration enforcement, federal aid conditions and election rules.

week.text: U.S. aid to Israel of about $4 billion a year will end after this year, President Trump said Tuesday, adding that Israel can still buy American weapons.
week.detail: In a phone interview with Fox News Channel's "Fox & Friends" on Election Day, Trump said he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to it months ago, that Netanyahu proposed it, and that the U.S. would "help Israel if they need it." He did not say how the cutoff would work. The current 2016 memorandum of understanding provides $3.8 billion a year ($3.3 billion in military financing and $500 million for missile defense) through 2028, and the money is appropriated by Congress. Netanyahu's office declined to comment Tuesday.
week.why: Israel is the largest recipient of U.S. military aid, and ending it would reverse a decades-old commitment.

week.text: Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz was hit Monday by limited U.S. "defensive" strikes on surface-to-air missiles used against U.S. aircraft, U.S. officials said.
week.detail: A U.S. official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the strikes targeted "Iranians using surface to air missiles against U.S. assets"; Iranian state TV reported explosions on the island. The strikes appeared limited rather than a return to full hostilities, AP reported, and came on the eve of the midterms after President Trump had said the U.S. would not launch new strikes before them. The Wall Street Journal first reported the strikes. The administration was last known to have attacked in early September; a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian oil continues and a third aircraft carrier is heading to the region. Hours earlier, Vice President JD Vance said he and Trump "feel pretty good" about a possible negotiated settlement; Qatari mediators held two rounds of talks with Iran last week.
week.why: It is the first known U.S. strike on Iran in about two months, as talks to end the war continue.
